nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Summer light and warmth drive growth from the lowland forests up to the alpine meadows.

nodes.name: Winter snow
nodes.desc: Deep mountain snow covers the high meadows for months and pushes grazers down into the forest; meltwater feeds the slopes in spring.

nodes.name: Heavy rainfall
nodes.desc: Moist air from the Black Sea brings the high precipitation that mountain firs need, over 1,000 mm a year.

nodes.name: Mountain soil and leaf litter
nodes.desc: Forest litter and mountain soils hold the nutrients that trees and meadow plants draw on.

nodes.name: Fungi and soil microbes
nodes.desc: Break down fallen leaves, wood, dung and carcasses, returning nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Oriental beech
nodes.desc: A dominant broadleaf tree of the Caucasus mid-mountain forests; its nuts feed boar and rodents.

nodes.name: Nordmann fir
nodes.desc: A tall mountain conifer growing at roughly 900 to 2,200 m. The Caucasus reserve was founded in 1924 partly to protect its giant firs.

nodes.name: Pedunculate oak
nodes.desc: A lowland and foothill oak whose acorns are a rich autumn food for bears, boar and rodents.

nodes.name: Common hazel
nodes.desc: A very widely recorded understory shrub whose nuts are eaten by boar, squirrels and mice.

nodes.name: Alpine meadow grasses and herbs
nodes.desc: Summer grassland above the treeline where chamois, tur, deer and bison graze.

nodes.name: European bison
nodes.desc: The Caucasian wisent was shot out by 1927; free-ranging herds now live again in the forests of the Western Caucasus. They graze grasses and herbs and browse shoots and bark.

nodes.name: Red deer
nodes.desc: A large forest and meadow herbivore of the Caucasus mountains, taken by wolves and bears.

nodes.name: Chamois
nodes.desc: Grazes highland grasses and herbs in summer and eats conifer bark and needles in winter, moving down to forest as snow deepens.

nodes.name: West Caucasian tur
nodes.desc: A wild goat found only in the western half of the Caucasus, living on steep, rocky mountain slopes and meadows.

nodes.name: Wild boar
nodes.desc: An omnivore of the forests that roots for acorns, nuts and other foods, and is itself prey for large carnivores.

nodes.name: Eurasian red squirrel
nodes.desc: The most recorded mammal near the site; eats hazelnuts and seeds in the forest canopy.

nodes.name: Yellow-necked mouse
nodes.desc: A forest rodent that eats nuts, acorns and seeds, and is food for foxes, buzzards and bears.

nodes.name: Red fox
nodes.desc: A flexible hunter and scavenger that takes rodents and squirrels and feeds on carcasses.

nodes.name: Common buzzard
nodes.desc: A raptor of forest edges and meadows that hunts rodents and other small animals.

nodes.name: Hooded crow
nodes.desc: An opportunistic bird that cleans up carrion left by larger predators.

nodes.name: Brown bear
nodes.desc: Mostly vegetarian, eating roots, nuts and acorns, but also takes rodents, boar and hoofed animals, and scavenges carrion in spring.

nodes.name: Gray wolf
nodes.desc: A pack-hunting predator of mountain ungulates such as deer and wild goats.

nodes.name: Persian leopard
nodes.desc: Reintroduced in 2016 and 2018 into the Caucasus Biosphere Reserve from a breeding centre in Sochi; chamois and boar are known prey of the subspecies.
